title: Growth-ratio bound for balls in the Cayley graph of the fundamental group of a spherical manifold
author: Ilya Alekseev, Ivan Nasonov, Gaiane Panina
work: Affine transverse foliations in sphere bundles
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Lemma 14 (source label 'lemmaNonAm'): in the Cayley graph of the fundamental group of the manifold, for every radius R > 2 the ratio of the number of vertices in the sphere of radius R to the number of vertices in the ball of radius R-1 is at most twice the vertex degree minus one. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete covering argument rather than a counting exercise: it fixes an arbitrary vertex in the annulus between the two balls, exhibits a neighbour in the smaller ball (an ancestor obtained from the fundamental domain adjacent to the vertex), deduces from that construction that at most degree-minus-one edges leave the smaller ball for the sphere, and combines the resulting edge count with the degree bound to produce exactly the stated ratio. The lemma is the quantitative input of the paper's estimate of the expected weight of an essential vertex, and the argument mixes the geometry of the fundamental domain with the combinatorics of the Cayley graph, which is research-level geometric group theory rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.
